content: 1. The RAND/UCLA appropriateness method user’s manual was published by the RAND Corporation in Santa Monica, California, in 2001. This manual provides a structured methodology for assessing the appropriateness of medical and healthcare interventions. 2. A mixed-methods study conducted by Straus SE, Moore JE, Uka S, Marquez C, and Gulmezoglu AM in 2013 explored the determinants of implementing maternal health guidelines in Kosovo. The findings were published in the journal Implementation Science. 3. Vogel JP, Moore JE, Timmings C, Khan S, Khan DN, Defar A, and colleagues identified barriers, facilitators, and priorities for implementing WHO maternal and perinatal health guidelines in four lower-income countries. This research was part of the GREAT Network and was published in PLOS One in 2016. 4. The 11th revision of the International Classification of Diseases (ICD) was released by the World Health Organization in Geneva in 2018. It serves as the global standard for diagnostic health information. 5. Ganatra B, Gerdts C, Rossier C, Johnson BR Jr, Tunçalp Ö, Assifi A, and others used a Bayesian hierarchical model to estimate global, regional, and subregional classifications of abortions by safety from 2010 to 2014. Their findings were published in The Lancet in 2017. 6. Say L, Chou D, Gemmill A, Tunçalp Ö, Moller AB, Daniels J, and colleagues conducted a systematic analysis of global causes of maternal death, which was published in The Lancet Global Health. 7. The Guttmacher Institute in New York published a report in 2016 on adolescents’ need for and use of abortion services in developing countries. 8. The World Health Organization released technical and policy guidance for health systems on safe abortion in Geneva in 2012. 9. Bartlett LA, Berg CJ, Shulman HB, Zane SB, Green CA, Whitehead S, and others identified risk factors for mortality related to legal induced abortion in the United States. Their study was published in Obstetrics & Gynecology in 2004. 10. Chae S, Desai S, Crowell M, Sedgh G, and Singh S examined the characteristics of women obtaining induced abortions in selected lowand middle-income countries. Their findings were published in PLOS One in 2017. 11. The United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs published a report in 2014 on abortion policies and reproductive health around the world. 12. Bayer L, Cheetham N, and Robbins S provided a global snapshot of youth and unsafe abortion in a report published by Advocates for Youth in Washington, DC, in 2011. 13. Berer M discussed the parameters of change in national laws and unsafe abortion in a 2004 article in Reproductive Health Matters. 14. Jewkes R, Rees H, Dickson K, Brown H, and Levin J analyzed the impact of age on the epidemiology of incomplete abortions in South Africa following legislative changes. Their findings were published in BJOG in 2005. 15. The United Nations Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women issued General Recommendation No. 35 on gender-based violence against women in 2017, updating General Recommendation No. 19. 16. The World Health Organization published a report in 2015 on the roles of health workers in providing safe abortion care and post-abortion contraception. 17. The 2005 World Health Report, titled Make Every Mother and Child Count, was published by the World Health Organization in Geneva. 18. The World Contraception Day Coalition released a framework for action on unplanned pregnancies in 2014, emphasizing global perspectives. 19. The World Health Organization published a clinical practice handbook for safe abortion in 2014. 20. An interagency statement on preventing gender-biased sex selection was released by the World Health Organization in 2011. 21. Renner RM, de Guzman A, and Brahmi D reviewed abortion care for adolescent and young women in a 2014 article in the International Journal of Gynecology & Obstetrics. 22. A systematic review on abortion care for adolescents and young women was published by Ipas in Chapel Hill, NC, in 2013. 23. The WHO strategic approach to strengthening sexual and reproductive health policies and programs was published in 2007. 24. Van Look PFA and Cottingham J discussed the WHO’s safe abortion guidance document in a 2013 article in the American Journal of Public Health. 25. Comendant R, Sagaidac I, and Hodorogea S highlighted achievements in sexual and reproductive health and rights in Moldova, focusing on improved access and quality of abortion services. Their findings were published in Entre Nous in 2016. 26. The World Health Organization released a fact sheet on sexually transmitted infections (STIs) in 2016. 27. Torrone EA, Morrison CS, Chen PL, Kwok C, Francis SC, and colleagues conducted a meta-analysis on the prevalence of STIs and bacterial vaginosis among women in sub-Saharan Africa. Their findings were published in PLOS Medicine in 2018. 28. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control published an annual epidemiological report on chlamydia for 2015. 29. Satterwhite CL, Torrone E, Meites E, Dunne EF, Mahajan R, Ocfemia MC, and others provided prevalence and incidence estimates of STIs among US women and men in a 2013 article in Sexually Transmitted Diseases. 30. Kleppa E, Holmen SD, Lillebo K, Kjetland EF, Gundersen SG, Taylor M, and colleagues studied the association between cervical ectopy, STIs, and HIV in high school students in rural South Africa. Their findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2015. 31. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention published a report on sexually transmitted disease surveillance in 2016. 32. Kågesten A, Gibbs S, Blum RW, Moreau C, Chandra-Mouli V, Herbert A, and colleagues conducted a systematic review on factors shaping gender attitudes in early adolescence globally. Their findings were published in PLOS One in 2016. 33. The World Health Organization released a global health sector strategy on STIs for 2016–2021, aiming to end STIs. 34. The WHO published recommendations for the prevention and treatment of HIV and other STIs among men who have sex with men and transgender people in 2011. 35. The WHO also released recommendations for the prevention and treatment of HIV and other STIs among sex workers in lowand middle-income countries in 2012. 36. Freeman EE, Weiss HA, Glynn JR, Cross PL, Whitworth JA, and Hayes RJ conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the role of herpes simplex virus 2 in increasing HIV acquisition. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2006. 37. Sexton J, Garnett G, and Rottingen JA used meta-analysis and meta-regression to interpret the variability in the impact of STIs on HIV susceptibility. Their findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2005. 38. Gottlieb SL, Low N, Newman LM, Bolan G, Kamb M, and Broutet N emphasized the need for STI vaccines in a 2014 article in Vaccine. 39. Johnson HL, Ghanem KG, Zenilman JM, and Erbelding EJ studied the association between STIs and adverse pregnancy outcomes among women attending public STI clinics. Their findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2011. 40. Newman L, Kamb M, Hawkes S, Gomez G, Say L, Seuc A, and colleagues analyzed global estimates of syphilis in pregnancy and associated adverse outcomes. Their findings were published in PLOS Medicine in 2013.
